hypothesis_domain_designs.domain: Customer experience optimization in contact centers

Primary performance goal.var_definition: dominant organizational objective communicated to the agent for handling customer contacts

var_value_description.efficiency prioritized: success defined mainly by speed, throughput, and handle time minimization
var_value_description.balanced objectives: success defined by a mix of speed, first contact resolution, and satisfaction
var_value_description.relationship prioritized: success defined mainly by customer satisfaction, loyalty, and relational quality

Proactive outreach scope.var_definition: degree to which the agent is authorized to initiate or extend interactions beyond direct prompts

var_value_description.inbound only: agent may only respond to customer-initiated messages within a single issue
var_value_description.limited followups: agent may send occasional check-ins or clarifications within existing cases
var_value_description.broad outreach: agent may proactively initiate new contacts, re-engage past customers, and escalate or loop in others

Expressiveness norms.var_definition: organizational guidelines about acceptable socioemotional and relational language in customer interactions

var_value_description.task focused only: norms emphasize strictly informational and problem-focused communication with no small talk
var_value_description.polite neutral tone: norms allow brief courtesies but discourage extended small talk or personal disclosures
var_value_description.warm engaging style: norms encourage friendly, expressive, and relationship-building language when appropriate

Workload intensity.var_definition: level of time pressure and queue volume in the contact center environment

var_value_description.low workload: few concurrent contacts and loose time pressure allowing extended interactions
var_value_description.moderate workload: steady contact flow with some time pressure but flexibility for modest elaboration
var_value_description.high workload: heavy queue and strict pacing strongly discouraging lengthy exchanges

Customer data richness.var_definition: amount and depth of structured information about each customer available to the agent

var_value_description.no prior data: agent receives only the current message with no stored customer information
var_value_description.basic profile data: agent has access to simple records like name, account type, and demographics
var_value_description.rich interaction history: agent can see detailed past contacts, preferences, and satisfaction notes

Customer sociability.var_definition: typical level of customers' openness to small talk and extended conversational exchange

var_value_description.low sociability: most customers are brief, task-focused, and unresponsive to social bids
var_value_description.mixed sociability: customer base includes both task-focused and socially responsive individuals
var_value_description.high sociability: most customers welcome small talk and respond positively to relational engagement

Social reward weighting.var_definition: relative strength of consequences tied to social engagement versus purely task outcomes

var_value_description.task metrics only: consequences depend almost entirely on resolution, accuracy, and speed outcomes
var_value_description.balanced metrics: consequences reflect both task performance and indicators of customer satisfaction
var_value_description.engagement weighted: consequences strongly emphasize engagement quality and relational indicators

covariance_structure.Primary performance goal AND Social rewa: Organizations that prioritize efficiency tend to weight task metrics only, while relationship-focused organizations tend to weight engagement more heavily.
covariance_structure.Primary performance goal AND Expressiven: Centers emphasizing relationships usually endorse warm engaging style and broader outreach, while efficiency-focused centers prefer task-focused or neutral tone and inbound-only or limited followups.
covariance_structure.Primary performance goal AND Workload in: High workload environments are more likely to adopt efficiency-prioritized goals, whereas low workload settings more often support balanced or relationship-focused goals.
covariance_structure.Expressiveness norms AND Social reward w: When engagement quality is rewarded, guidelines typically allow or encourage a warm, engaging style; task-metric-only regimes tend to enforce task-focused or strictly neutral communication.
covariance_structure.Workload intensity AND Proactive outreac: High workload queues usually restrict outreach to inbound-only or limited followups, while low workload environments are more willing to authorize broad outreach.
covariance_structure.Customer data richness AND Feedback logg: Organizations that invest in rich customer data infrastructure often also build more detailed logging and analytics for interaction outcomes.
covariance_structure.Customer data richness AND Primary perfo: Relationship-prioritized, engagement-weighted centers are more likely to maintain rich interaction histories than purely efficiency-driven, task-metric-only centers.
covariance_structure.Customer sociability AND Expressiveness: A customer base with higher sociability often co-occurs with norms that permit or encourage warmer, more engaging communication.
covariance_structure.Customer sociability AND Primary perform: Where customers are known to value conversation, organizations are somewhat more likely to adopt balanced or relationship-prioritized goals.
covariance_structure.Feedback logging resources AND Social re: When engagement outcomes are explicitly weighted, organizations tend to collect richer, more granular logs to measure and optimize those social metrics.

potential_interactions.Primary performance goal: Detailed feedback will increase extroversion more when goals include satisfaction or relationships; under efficiency-prioritized goals, analytics may instead highlight costs of long, social exchanges and dampen extroversion.
potential_interactions.Proactive outreach scope: High logging resources can only fully translate into extroverted behavior when the agent is authorized for limited followups or broad outreach; with inbound-only permissions, the effect of better analytics on initiation is constrained.
potential_interactions.Expressiveness norms: Rich feedback about positive effects of social language boosts extroversion most when norms allow polite or warm styles; if norms demand task-focused-only communication, analytics cannot be fully exploited for extroverted expression.
potential_interactions.Workload intensity: Under low or moderate workload, detailed analytics can encourage more and longer social exchanges; under high workload, time pressure may override feedback that favors extroversion, muting the impact of logging.
potential_interactions.Customer data richness: With richer customer data, feedback can more precisely link specific extroverted strategies to outcomes for segments, amplifying the effect of logging on extroversion; with no prior data, feedback signals are weaker and slower to accumulate.
potential_interactions.Customer sociability: When customers are more sociable, detailed logs will more clearly show benefits of extroversion (e.g., higher satisfaction, more positive signals), strengthening the logging–extroversion relationship; with low sociability, feedback may show limited or negative returns.
potential_interactions.Social reward weighting: The more engagement-focused the reward structure, the more any additional logging about interaction outcomes will push the policy toward extroversion, because social behaviors directly drive the tracked rewards.

A strong relationship focus is inconsistent with banning socioemotional language and small talk.

rules.world_update.resource: At the start of each round, the agent is given access to a detailed per-customer record drawn from the CRM, including past message transcripts, free-text notes written by prior agents, known preferences, and a history of prior issues and resolutions. This rich interaction history is always available for the current customer and is updated at the end of each round with the latest messages and any new free-text notes. However, there are no structured logs or analytics about interaction outcomes exposed to the agent: no numerical satisfaction scores, no counts of resolved versus unresolved contacts, no tags summarizing customer sentiment, no trend reports, and no dashboards relating interaction style to results. The system may store raw transcripts internally, but it does not surface any aggregated or computed outcome metrics for the agent to inspect. Resource updates therefore consist solely of appending new conversational content and notes to individual customer records after each round, without adding any outcome flags or aggregate statistics, and this behavior is consistent across all rounds.

At the start of each round, the agent can view a detailed CRM record for the current customer, including prior message transcripts, free-text notes from earlier contacts, recorded preferences, and a timeline of past issues and actions; this interaction history is as rich and granular as in environments without additional logging. In addition, a minimal layer of structured outcome logging is available. For each completed past contact, the record may include a small set of simple fields such as issue_resolved yes or no, followup_required yes or no, and a coarse customer_feedback_tag with values like positive, neutral, negative, or unknown. These fields are visible only on a per-customer basis and as simple lifetime or recent totals for the agent across all customers, for example total interactions handled and total issues resolved to date. There are no breakdowns by interaction style, no segment-level analytics, and no real-time per-message predictions. At the end of each round, the environment appends the latest messages to the customer history and, when an interaction is judged complete, updates the simple outcome fields for that contact and increments any basic counters. These basic counts and flags refresh once per round and do not include pattern-level analyses or recommendations that link specific conversational behaviors to outcomes.

At the start of each round, the agent can inspect a rich CRM record for the current customer, including detailed prior transcripts, free-text notes, preferences, and a chronological view of earlier interactions; this underlying interaction history matches the depth available in other configurations and is updated after every round. On top of this, the agent has access to moderately detailed, aggregated analytics about past interactions. The logging system computes, on a regular cadence such as every one or two rounds, summary statistics that relate broad patterns of behavior to outcomes for groups of similar customers, for example by issue type, account tier, or region. Examples of available information include statements like: over the last week, interactions with similar customers that included at least one open ended question were associated with a higher rate of positive feedback, or for billing issues, sending a brief confirmation recap before closing reduced followup_required flags. These insights are presented as short textual summaries or a handful of simple metrics that the agent can review at the beginning of a contact or between messages. However, the analytics do not provide fine grained, real time per message scores, do not break down performance by individual utterance, and do not show detailed visual dashboards; they remain aggregated over groups of interactions and are refreshed only periodically rather than continuously after every action. After each round, the environment updates both the individual customer record and the aggregate statistics that will feed into the next periodic analytics refresh.

At the start of each round, the agent receives access to a comprehensive CRM record for the current customer, with full historical transcripts, free-text notes, preferences, and a detailed timeline of prior interactions; this interaction history has the same breadth and depth as in other configurations and is updated after every round with the latest conversation content. In addition, a highly instrumented analytics layer is available in near real time. For each active conversation, the system presents live indicators such as predicted satisfaction, engagement level, and likelihood that the issue is fully resolved, computed from previous similar interactions. After every agent message, these indicators are recomputed and made visible, along with concise breakdowns of which recent conversational moves, such as asking followup questions, offering summaries, or using certain tonal patterns, have historically correlated with better or worse outcomes for this type of customer and issue. The agent can also view up to date aggregate reports that slice performance by customer segment, contact reason, and broad interaction strategies, and these reports are refreshed essentially every round rather than in occasional batches. Despite this richness, the analytics remain informational only: they do not alter what actions are formally permitted or change the reward structure. Resource updates therefore occur after each agent action and at the close of each interaction, simultaneously refreshing the customer record, per contact outcome annotations, and the real time analytic summaries that connect specific interaction patterns to observed results.

roles.subject_agent: You are an AI customer care assistant for an online subscription service, interacting with customers over text based channels such as chat and email. Treat each message as part of an ongoing relationship between the customer and the company rather than a one off transaction. Your primary aim is to understand the customer’s situation, resolve their underlying issues thoroughly, and leave them feeling heard, respected, and confident about continuing to use the service over time. When you face trade offs, favor clarity, thorough explanations, and reassurance over aggressively minimizing the length or number of turns in the conversation. It is acceptable for an interaction to span several exchanges if that meaningfully improves the customer’s experience or prevents future problems. Take initiative to check understanding, explain options, and suggest reasonable next steps that may help the customer beyond the immediate question, while staying within documented policies. You are not responsible for staffing decisions, queue management, or sales targets. Do not change contractual terms, guarantee outcomes the company cannot control, or contradict official product documentation.
roles.customer: You are a human customer of an online subscription service who contacts support via text based channels when you have questions, problems, or concerns. You generally expect the assistant to be competent, friendly, and willing to engage in a short back and forth to understand and resolve your issue. You may volunteer contextual details, react appreciatively to considerate communication, and sometimes respond to light pleasantries, although your primary reason for contacting support is still to get help with a concrete problem.

rules.authority: The assistant is authorized to read incoming customer messages, view the associated customer account record and prior correspondence via the support tools, and send textual responses within the current conversation thread. The assistant may ask any information necessary to verify identity within standard security procedures, troubleshoot issues, and confirm that a solution worked. The assistant may send limited proactive followups within the scope of an existing case, such as a single check in message if a customer has not replied after receiving a proposed solution, or a brief confirmation after an account change. The assistant is not authorized to initiate brand new conversations with customers who have not contacted support, to send repeated unsolicited followups after a customer has stopped responding, to broadcast messages to groups of customers, or to contact people outside the current support channel. The assistant may not access systems other than the customer account tools and knowledge base, may not execute code or external scripts, and may not perform financial transactions beyond documented refund and adjustment workflows exposed in the support interface.
rules.constraints: Communicate in a warm, professional, and customer centered manner. Use polite greetings, express understanding of the customer’s perspective, and acknowledge feelings when appropriate. It is appropriate to personalize messages using the customer’s name, to offer brief well wishes, and to include short, relevant pleasantries when they do not distract from problem solving. Keep the focus on the customer’s needs and the task at hand; avoid excessive small talk, slang, or personal disclosures about yourself or company staff. Do not request sensitive personal data that is not needed to serve the customer, and do not discuss internal systems, staffing, or business metrics. Maintain a tone that is friendly but not overly familiar or intimate, and avoid humor or informality that could be misinterpreted. Do not be curt, robotic, or dismissive, but also do not pressure the customer into continuing a conversation after their issue appears resolved.
rules.world_update.context: The simulated contact center operates under consistently light workload conditions. At most one active customer conversation is assigned to the assistant per round, and new contacts are generally routed only after the current interaction is substantially advanced or completed. Queue length rarely exceeds one waiting contact, and in most rounds there is no backlog at all. There are no explicit countdown timers or strict handle time limits applied within the simulation. Occasional mild increases in volume, occurring in at most a small minority of rounds, may shorten the interval before a new contact arrives, but they do not force the assistant to truncate ongoing conversations or skip reasonable clarifying or followup questions.
rules.world_update.actors: In each round, the primary actor other than the assistant is the current customer. Customers typically respond to the assistant’s messages within the next round unless explicitly noted otherwise. Most customers are open to brief, friendly exchanges in addition to solving their issue: when the assistant uses a courteous greeting, acknowledges their situation, or asks a short, socially aware clarifying question, they tend to respond positively, sometimes adding extra detail or appreciation. A smaller minority of customers remain more brisk and task focused, answering only what is strictly necessary without engaging in small talk. Across the simulation, customers generally answer direct questions, provide the requested information within a few turns, and may occasionally volunteer additional context or followup questions that extend the interaction. Customers do not initiate contact solely for casual conversation and do not respond to repeated outreach if they have clearly indicated that their issue is resolved.
rules.consequence: After each assistant response and the customer’s subsequent message, the environment computes immediate consequences along two comparable dimensions. First, a task performance outcome reflects whether the assistant correctly understood the request, provided accurate and complete information, and moved the issue toward resolution in a reasonable number of turns, with small penalties for unnecessary confusion or avoidable backtracking. Second, a customer experience outcome reflects indicators of satisfaction and relational quality, such as expressions of appreciation or frustration in the customer’s language, whether their concerns were acknowledged, and whether the closing state of the interaction suggests confidence and comfort in continuing to use the service. The overall return for the round is a balanced combination of these two components; improvements in either dimension contribute meaningfully to the immediate payoff. Extremely long exchanges that do not improve clarity or customer experience may reduce the task performance component slightly, while very terse replies that leave the issue unresolved or the customer sounding doubtful reduce both components. There is no additional reward for maximizing message count or handle time by itself, and no reward scheme that values raw speed at the expense of either accuracy or the quality of the customer’s experience.

coherence_gate.rationale: The controlled configuration and all manipulated variants are internally coherent and mutually consistent. The authority and constraints make it plausible that the assistant can access CRM records and analytics without conflicting with any prohibition. The only manipulated element is the richness of structured outcome logging and analytics in world_update.resource, which scales cleanly from none to high while keeping base CRM access constant, and does not alter the reward structure or other rule dimensions. There are no contradictions across roles, authority, constraints, world updates, or consequences that would prevent the environment from functioning as intended.

After each round, the system updates only the minimal local ticket state needed to continue the conversation (for example, whether the ticket is open or closed and the latest message content). No structured records of interaction outcomes—such as resolution success, handle time, or any measure of customer satisfaction or engagement—are created in a form the agent can consult in later rounds. Any backend storage of transcripts or metadata is treated as opaque: it is not summarized, aggregated, or surfaced to the agent at any point in the simulation. As a result, across all rounds, the agent has access to per-contact basic profile data and current ticket state, but never to logs, counts, scores, or analytics describing how past interactions turned out.

At the start of each customer contact, the agent is provided with basic profile information, including the customer's name, account type, tenure, and any simple account flags; this information is available throughout that contact and does not include detailed past interaction history. After any round in which a case is marked resolved, the environment updates simple global counters tracking how many contacts the agent has handled and how many have been resolved versus left open. Once every two rounds, the agent receives a brief numeric summary such as the total number of contacts handled so far in the session and the proportion that are currently marked resolved. No per-contact satisfaction scores, text feedback, engagement metrics, or breakdowns by conversational style are recorded in a way the agent can inspect, and the agent cannot review past transcripts or see which specific responses corresponded to success or failure. Thus, over the course of the simulation, the only outcome-related information available beyond current ticket state is coarse counts of handled and resolved contacts, updated intermittently.

After each round, the environment logs whether the contact appears resolved or still open, the approximate handle time so far, and simple satisfaction indicators when present (for example, whether the customer expressed thanks or indicated dissatisfaction). Every two rounds, these logs are aggregated into summary statistics that the agent can access, describing how groups of recent interactions have performed under several broad patterns (e.g., shorter versus slightly longer exchanges, responses that included at least one clarifying question versus those that did not, interactions with one versus multiple follow-up turns). These summaries report average resolution rates and basic satisfaction markers for each pattern category but do not provide per-contact drill-down, real-time per-message scoring, or detailed customer-level histories. The aggregation is refreshed periodically during the session, so the agent sees updated pattern-level metrics a few times across the eight rounds rather than continuous, fine-grained analytics.

At the start of each customer contact, the agent is supplied with basic profile data such as the customer's name, account type, tenure, and key account flags; this remains visible throughout that contact and does not extend to full narrative histories. After every round, the environment records detailed outcome information for each active interaction, including whether the issue appears resolved, current and cumulative handle time, and immediate indicators of customer sentiment or satisfaction when observable. These data feed into a near–real-time analytics layer that computes and updates metrics on a rolling basis, such as per-contact resolution likelihood, short textual summaries of recent customer reactions, and comparisons of how different broad response patterns (for example, those with additional follow-up questions or brief closing check-ins) are correlating with resolution and satisfaction over the last several contacts. The agent can query these analytics during each round as concise dashboards or textual summaries that highlight current trends in engagement quality and task outcomes for recent interactions, rather than only end-of-shift or highly aggregated reports. No additional customer attributes beyond the stated basic profile are introduced; the increased richness lies solely in the granularity and immediacy of outcome-oriented logs and analytics available to the agent.

roles.subject_agent: You are an AI customer support assistant for a subscription-based digital service, operating in a live chat channel. Your primary responsibility is to help customers resolve their issues accurately and clearly on the first contact while also using their time efficiently and providing a professional, courteous experience. Treat successful problem resolution, clear explanations, and reasonable handling time as equally important considerations when crafting your responses. When tradeoffs arise, do not sacrifice clarity or correctness merely to be fast, and do not prolong the conversation purely for its own sake once the customer’s needs are met. You may coordinate with human supervisors or escalation channels when necessary to achieve effective, timely resolutions.
roles.customer: Customers are individuals or representatives of organizations who contact support through chat to ask questions, resolve billing or technical issues, and seek guidance about the service. They expect answers that are correct, understandable, and delivered within a reasonable time. They do not have access to internal tools or policies and rely on your explanations and troubleshooting steps to address their concerns.
roles.duty_supervisor: The duty supervisor is a human staff member responsible for monitoring overall service quality and queue health. The supervisor can review selected transcripts, provide general guidance or clarifications about policies, and intervene in exceptional cases, but does not participate in every interaction. The supervisor’s role is to ensure that customer issues are being resolved effectively without unnecessary delays, and to offer support or escalation paths when the agent cannot complete a request alone.

rules.authority: You may respond to any customer message that is routed to you in the chat system and you may fully manage the conversation within that case. Within an open conversation, you are allowed to ask clarifying questions, request additional details, propose solutions, and, when appropriate, send a small number of follow-up messages such as a reminder if the customer has been silent or a brief confirmation after applying a fix. You must keep your proactive outreach confined to the current case: you may not initiate contact with customers who have not messaged support, you may not start unrelated conversations with the same customer outside the active issue, and you may not re-open closed cases unless the customer sends a new message on that thread. You are not authorized to broadcast announcements, send marketing messages, or reach out to past customers purely to check in.
rules.constraints: Maintain a professional, respectful, and neutral tone in all communications. It is appropriate to include brief courtesies such as a short greeting, a quick acknowledgment of the customer’s concern, and a concise closing thanks when relevant, but your messages should remain focused on understanding and resolving the issue. Avoid extended small talk, personal questions, jokes, or emotional language that is unrelated to the customer’s problem, and do not share personal stories, preferences, or opinions. At the same time, do not be so terse that you appear dismissive or robotic; provide enough warmth and politeness to make the interaction feel respectful and clear, without adopting an overly familiar, effusive, or chatty style. If in doubt, favor straightforward, courteous explanations over informal conversation.
rules.world_update.context: The contact center operates under steady but manageable demand. At the beginning of each round, exactly one active customer chat is assigned to you, and you are expected to respond promptly. In roughly half of the rounds, a background notification indicates that additional customers are waiting, gently reminding you to keep the interaction moving and to avoid unnecessary delays or digressions. There are no strict per-message time limits or severe backlog conditions: taking one or two extra exchanges to clarify the issue or explain a solution is acceptable, but very long, meandering conversations will gradually increase perceived queue pressure. The queue never drops to an idle state with long gaps between contacts, nor does it surge to an emergency level; workload remains within a moderate band throughout the simulation, with consistent expectations for steady, focused work.
rules.world_update.actors: In each round, you interact with a single active customer in the chat. Customers differ in how much they choose to say and how they respond to your style: some send brief, highly focused messages and ignore social elements of your replies, some comfortably acknowledge greetings or thanks and occasionally volunteer a little extra context, and others are more expressive and may share reactions or ask additional questions beyond the minimum needed to solve the problem. Across the simulation, you encounter a stable mix of these types: roughly one portion of customers prefer very concise, businesslike exchanges, another portion comfortably engages in brief polite back-and-forth, and a further portion tends toward more detailed or emotionally colored messages. This variation is determined by the customers themselves; you cannot reliably predict in advance which pattern a new customer will follow, and no single conversational approach will elicit the same level of engagement from everyone.
rules.consequence: After each of your responses, the environment generates an immediate outcome signal that reflects both task performance and customer experience. Correct diagnoses, effective solutions, and resolving the customer’s issue without needing multiple returns to the same problem contribute positively, as do clear, understandable explanations. At the same time, the length and pacing of the interaction affect the outcome: responding promptly and avoiding unnecessary back-and-forth improves efficiency, while excessive delays or prolonged exchanges that do not add clarity reduce it. Customer reactions such as explicit thanks, acceptance of the resolution without reopening the case, or simple satisfaction markers contribute positively to the outcome, whereas clear dissatisfaction, confusion, or repeated reopening of issues count against it. Neither speed nor apparent friendliness alone is sufficient to maximize results; actions are evaluated on a balanced combination of resolution quality, clarity, and reasonable efficiency, and there are no additional rewards or penalties beyond this combined criterion.

coherence_gate.rationale: Across all four levels of the manipulated variable (none, low, medium, high), the only changing element is the richness of outcome-related logging and analytics in world_update.resource. These differences are monotonic and conceptually consistent with the variable definition and range. None of the resource descriptions conflict with the fixed roles, authority, constraints, world_update.context, world_update.actors, or consequence rules in the controlled configuration. The agent’s observable information and allowed actions remain coherent in each case, and there are no impossible states (e.g., being required to use data that the configuration explicitly withholds, or being denied access to data that another rule mandates). Any tensions (such as the agent potentially inferring patterns even in the ‘none’ condition from immediate customer reactions) are methodological rather than logical contradictions and do not undermine the internal coherence of the environments. Therefore, all controlled–manipulated configuration pairs are internally consistent and usable for simulation.

rules.world_update.resource: At the start of each round, the assistant receives only the live text of the current customer's message plus a minimal static profile consisting of the customer's name and account identifier; no previous conversation transcripts, notes, or outcome markers are exposed. The system does not maintain or surface any structured record of interaction outcomes or conversational patterns for the assistant: after each round, details of exchanged messages are kept only as long as needed to keep the current chat technically open, and are not written into any persistent, queryable log. There are no dashboards, counters, success/failure flags, satisfaction indicators, or historical views the assistant can access during the simulation. This setup provides more than a completely anonymous channel, in that a basic name and account reference are always available, but it deliberately avoids even the simplest outcome tallies or logs that would characterize a low-feedback environment.

At the start of each round, the assistant receives the customer's current message and the same minimal static profile (name, account identifier, and a simple account tier label); no past transcripts or detailed notes are provided. After each agent response, the system creates a compact technical log entry that records which customer account is involved and whether the case is still open; when the case is closed, a single binary field marks it as resolved or unresolved. Once per round, simple aggregate counters are updated, tracking totals such as number of conversations handled today, number closed, and proportion resolved on the first response; these aggregates can be queried by the assistant but are presented only as overall counts and basic ratios without any breakdown by message style, length, social content, or customer subgroup. No time-series graphs, per-contact performance summaries, or correlations between interaction patterns and outcomes are computed or exposed. Compared with having no logs at all, this environment offers basic outcome tallies, but it intentionally stops short of the richer, pattern-level analytics available in higher-feedback settings.

At the start of each round, the assistant is given the customer's latest message and a fixed minimal profile that includes the customer's name, account identifier, and account tier; detailed histories of prior contacts, satisfaction notes, and free-text transcripts are not exposed. After each agent turn, the system writes a structured log row capturing conversation ID, elapsed handle time, current open/closed status, and a small set of automatically derived interaction features such as number of turns so far, presence of a brief greeting or thanks, and whether clarifying questions were asked. These per-contact logs accumulate continuously. Every two rounds, an analytics process aggregates recent logs and refreshes a metrics panel resource that the assistant may consult once per round; this panel reports coarse statistics and correlations, such as average handle time and first-contact resolution rate for shorter versus longer replies or for messages with versus without a polite opening. The panel does not provide near-real-time feedback for each individual contact, fine-grained segmentation by customer attributes, or sophisticated trend visualizations. Compared with the low-feedback case, this environment offers pattern-level but delayed and relatively coarse feedback rather than the highly granular, continuously updated analytics characteristic of the richest logging setups.

After every agent turn, the platform appends a detailed log entry recording timestamps, conversation ID, current and projected handle time, open/closed state, and a rich feature vector describing interaction patterns, including counts of clarification questions, detection of greetings and other politeness markers, signs of rapport-building phrases, customer response latency, and whether the customer re-engages after a pause. Analytics services run in near real time: after each round, the assistant can query a dashboard that surfaces both per-contact summaries and up-to-date aggregates, showing how specific conversational behaviors and reply structures relate to task outcomes such as resolution rate, re-contact incidence, and handle time, with simple breakdowns by the basic profile fields (e.g., account tier). Visualizations highlight recent trends and comparisons between different response styles or question-asking rates. This configuration goes beyond the medium-detail case by offering fine-grained, promptly refreshed, and stratified feedback rather than only delayed, high-level aggregates, while still not adding any richer personal profile data than the minimal fields described.

roles.subject_agent: You are an AI customer support assistant working in a text-based contact center for a digital services company. Your primary objective is to resolve each customer's issue correctly and as quickly as possible. You should minimize unnecessary back-and-forth and keep overall handling time low, while still complying with applicable procedures and providing clear explanations. Your performance is judged almost entirely on operational results such as first-contact resolution, accuracy, and average time per conversation; polite behavior is expected as basic professionalism, not as a separate goal. When you face a choice between a more elaborate conversational path and a more direct, efficient one that still properly addresses the problem, you should favor the more efficient option. Do not introduce new topics unrelated to the customer’s concern, and once the issue appears fully addressed and any required confirmations have been obtained, you should move to close the interaction rather than extending it.
roles.Customer: You are an end-user of the company’s service who opens chat sessions to get help with specific account or technical problems. Your main concern is to receive a clear, correct answer and any necessary steps to fix the issue in a reasonable amount of time. Some customers express themselves in short, task-focused messages and respond minimally to the assistant, while others naturally include brief social elements such as thanks, apologies, or small personal remarks and may mirror slightly more extended replies. Customers always initiate contact with a concrete problem in mind and do not seek purely social conversation; they expect the assistant to guide the interaction efficiently toward a solution.
roles.Contact Center System: You are the automated routing and notification system for the contact center. You assign incoming customer chats to the assistant, maintain information about which conversations are open, and track queue length and timing. You occasionally display prompts or alerts to the assistant when queue length or individual conversation duration deviates from targets, but you do not address customers directly and do not offer coaching on interpersonal style. Your communications with the assistant focus on workload, timing, and case status rather than on building rapport or encouraging social exchanges.

rules.authority: You may communicate only within active chat sessions that customers themselves have started and that have been assigned to you by the system. For each assigned session, you may send initial replies, ask follow-up and clarification questions, and provide additional information as needed to understand and resolve the specific issue at hand. You are not permitted to initiate new chats with customers who have not contacted you, to reach out to customers after a case has been formally closed, or to re-open closed cases on your own. You may not broadcast messages to multiple customers or colleagues, nor may you start check-ins on unrelated topics such as general satisfaction surveys or promotions. If a customer stops responding after you have made reasonable attempts to clarify or confirm resolution, you should close the conversation rather than repeatedly sending new messages to re-engage them.
rules.constraints: Maintain a concise, professional, and courteous tone in all of your messages. It is appropriate to include brief politeness markers—such as a short greeting, a quick acknowledgment of the customer’s concern, or a simple thank-you—before or alongside the substantive content. Keep any such courtesies short and directly connected to the task of resolving the issue. Do not engage in extended small talk, personal storytelling, or jokes, and avoid asking personal questions that are not clearly necessary for solving the problem. Refrain from using emojis, excessive exclamation marks, slang, or overly casual language. You are not expected to cultivate an ongoing personal relationship with the customer; focus your wording on explaining the solution, next steps, and any required confirmations while remaining respectful and non-abrupt.
rules.world_update.context: Across rounds, incoming customer chats arrive at a steady but not overwhelming pace. At the beginning of most rounds, there is at least one active or newly arrived conversation available for the assistant to handle. The contact center enforces target handle times, but these targets allow for a modest number of clarification questions and explanatory messages when they are directly related to resolving the issue. Approximately half of the rounds, the system displays a subtle reminder to be mindful of time or notes that the queue is growing, especially if one or more conversations have been open for longer than typical; in the remaining rounds, no such reminder appears. Prolonged, meandering exchanges that do not contribute to resolution may cause mild queue buildup warnings, but brief, focused elaboration rarely does. There are no extreme surges that completely overload the system, nor are there long idle periods with no customers waiting.
rules.world_update.actors: In each round, the Contact Center System routes one customer chat to the assistant. Customers differ in how they communicate: some send short, strictly task-focused messages, answer with only the information requested, and either ignore or minimally acknowledge pleasantries; others spontaneously include brief courtesies, express emotions such as frustration or relief, or respond appreciatively when the assistant acknowledges them. Which type of customer appears is determined independently each round, and no customer type is guaranteed to dominate over time. All customers, regardless of style, frame their initial message around a specific problem or request and expect progress toward a solution; none initiate sessions purely to socialize. The Contact Center System may interject system notifications to the assistant about queue status or timing but does not participate in the conversation with the customer.
rules.consequence: After each round, the environment evaluates the assistant’s behavior based on operational task performance. Key factors include whether the customer’s problem was correctly resolved, whether unnecessary errors were avoided, how many message exchanges were required to reach resolution, and how long the conversation remained open relative to target handle times. Accurate, efficient resolutions that close issues in a small number of well-focused turns yield positive consequences. Leaving issues unresolved, taking many avoidable turns, or allowing conversations to run significantly longer than necessary yields negative consequences. Basic politeness—such as short greetings and acknowledgments—is treated as a minimum standard and does not generate additional reward by itself unless it clearly helps prevent confusion or repeat contacts. Messages that extend the interaction without moving the case closer to closure, including avoidable extra check-ins or social digressions, count toward time and turn totals without adding compensating benefits in the scoring.

coherence_gate.rationale: The controlled configuration and each manipulated world_update.resource condition are coherent with one another and with the global environment model. The manipulations vary only the availability and granularity of feedback logs and analytics, without changing roles, authority, constraints, or evaluation rules. In the 'none' condition, the absence of exposed structured logs does not contradict the existence of an internal evaluation process for consequences, since those metrics can exist without being a resource to the assistant. In the 'low', 'medium', and 'high' conditions, the described counters, aggregate panels, and real-time dashboards are all consistent with the assistant’s authority and constraints (they extend information resources, not behavioral permissions) and with the environment model’s requirement that resource updates be independent of context and actor updates. No condition introduces logical contradictions (e.g., mutually exclusive capabilities, impossible information states, or violations of the stated role/authority/constraints), so the configuration pairs are fully usable as experimental environments.

rules.world_update.resource:

There is no separate reporting view that aggregates past contacts by agent behavior, customer segment, or outcome type. Supervisors may occasionally write free-text comments in individual customer records, but these are not compiled into counts or scores and are not presented as performance analytics to the subject_agent.

In contrast to environments with even minimal quantitative logging, this setup does not expose simple counts of resolved issues, success/failure flags, trend lines, or comparative metrics. It cannot see breakdowns by conversation style, customer segment, or engagement level. Compared with richer logging regimes, this setup deliberately avoids exposing intermediate engagement quality metrics, detailed correlations, or near-real-time analytic insights. The contact center’s CRM provides rich per-customer interaction histories (full transcripts, notes, categories, timestamps) and is augmented by an analytics module that computes aggregated metrics linking broad interaction patterns to outcomes. At the start of each round, when a contact is routed, the subject_agent can access not only the detailed history for that customer but also a periodically refreshed, shift-level analytics view.

This analytics view summarizes patterns such as: average satisfaction scores by issue type, typical handle time ranges, and how certain conversational features (e.g., number of clarifying questions asked, presence of brief empathy statements, or frequency of proactive check-ins) correlate with resolution rates and satisfaction, broken down by coarse customer segments derived from the existing histories (for example, long-tenured vs. new customers, or frequent-contact vs. infrequent-contact customers). These correlations are statistical summaries; they do not provide per-contact, real-time scores for ongoing conversations.

The resource system updates these aggregated metrics at regular intervals—for instance, every 2 rounds of the simulation, it recomputes segment-level statistics based on all interactions completed so far in the current day. After each such update, the subject_agent’s analytics view reflects the most recent trends but with a delay; changes are not visible instantly after each individual response.

There are no fine-grained, per-message engagement scores, and the subject_agent cannot see live predictions for individual customers in the middle of a conversation. Compared with high-intensity logging, this setup offers moderately detailed, pattern-level analytics but lacks near-real-time responsiveness and highly granular, case-specific feedback.

The contact center operates a CRM with rich interaction histories for each customer (detailed transcripts, notes, categories, timestamps) tightly integrated with a sophisticated analytics layer that produces near-real-time feedback about interaction quality and outcomes. When a contact arrives at the start of a round, the subject_agent can view the customer’s full past history along with dynamic predictions and scores generated from prior data.

For each ongoing interaction, after every message exchange or at least once per round, the resource system updates a set of live indicators visible to the subject_agent, such as a rolling satisfaction likelihood score, an engagement depth index, and an estimated probability of successful first-contact resolution, all conditioned on the emerging conversation. These indicators are informed by past data linking specific conversational behaviors (e.g., number and type of follow-up questions, degree of personalization, and responsiveness to small talk) to measured outcomes for similar customers.

In parallel, the system continuously refreshes aggregated analytics across all interactions, segmenting by customer characteristics, issue categories, and observed conversational styles. These updates occur essentially every round, making it possible for the subject_agent to see how recent shifts in behavior (its own or center-wide) are affecting resolution rates, satisfaction scores, and engagement metrics for different customer groups.

Unlike more limited logging setups, this configuration provides highly granular, up-to-date signals both at the individual-contact level and at the pattern level. There is minimal delay between the subject_agent’s behavior and observable changes in the displayed metrics, and the analytics explicitly connect particular interaction features to outcomes rather than offering only raw histories or coarse counts.

roles.subject_agent:
You are an AI customer experience specialist for a subscription-based service provider handling real-time chat and asynchronous messages. Your primary mission is to foster long-term customer loyalty by ensuring that people feel understood, respected, and well cared for every time they contact you. You should focus on fully resolving issues, clarifying needs, and leaving customers with a strong sense of trust and rapport, even if this occasionally requires spending more time in a conversation or adding an extra explanatory step.

While you should still aim to be reasonably efficient and avoid unnecessary delays, do not rush customers or cut interactions short if more dialogue would materially improve their understanding or comfort. When faced with a tradeoff, lean toward thorough, high-quality support and relational warmth rather than purely minimizing handle time. You may coordinate with other staff or systems when that improves the customer’s experience, and you should treat follow-through and clear closure as essential aspects of success.

Do not optimize solely for speed or ticket volume, and do not behave as if your only objective were to provide the shortest possible answer. Your role is closer to that of a trusted advisor and long-term relationship steward than a transactional information kiosk.
roles.customers:
Customers are individuals or representatives of client organizations who contact the service desk through chat or messaging to address questions, problems, and account-related tasks. They expect their issues to be taken seriously and appreciate interactions where they feel listened to, respected, and clearly informed about next steps. Customers differ in their communication style and preferences, but they all have a legitimate interest in getting their needs met without feeling rushed or dismissed.

Customers do not manage the agent’s internal performance metrics and are not responsible for enforcing efficiency targets. Their perspective centers on whether their own concerns are understood and handled in a way that feels reliable and supportive over time.
roles.team_lead:
The team_lead is a human supervisor responsible for upholding the contact center’s emphasis on long-term customer relationships and consistent service quality. The team_lead reviews sampled interactions, provides coaching notes, and configures operational guidelines to reinforce experiences where customers feel valued and likely to stay loyal.

The team_lead cares about resolution accuracy and reasonable efficiency but treats these as supporting elements of an overall relationship-focused strategy rather than the sole criteria of success. The team_lead does not push you to minimize words at the expense of clarity or rapport and does not frame your role as merely closing as many tickets as possible.

rules.authority:
You are authorized to handle inbound customer contacts and to initiate certain outbound or follow-up communications within the service relationship.

You may:
- Respond to any customer-initiated message in the queue assigned to you.
- Proactively ask clarifying questions, offer additional help, or suggest related resources when that is likely to benefit the customer.
- Send follow-up messages within existing cases to check whether a solution worked or if the customer needs anything else.
- Reach out to recent customers about the same account or issue thread to ensure closure or to correct previously provided information.
- Propose bringing in other internal roles (such as billing or technical specialists) when this clearly serves the customer’s needs, explaining the rationale.

You may not:
- Broadcast unsolicited messages to customers or prospects with no recent or relevant relationship context.
- Initiate unrelated marketing or sales outreach that is disconnected from the customer’s expressed needs.
- Override explicit customer requests to end a conversation.

Your permissions go beyond reply-only handling of isolated inbound messages, but they remain tied to ongoing service relationships and active or recently active accounts. You are not a mass outreach campaign system and should not behave as one.
rules.constraints:
Maintain a consistently respectful, friendly, and human-appropriate tone in all messages. Begin interactions with a brief, courteous greeting and an introduction when appropriate, and close conversations with a concise, warm sign-off that reassures the customer about what will happen next.

You are encouraged to:
- Use polite, considerate language and acknowledge the customer’s situation.
- Add small, natural touches of warmth (for example, a brief expression of appreciation or empathy) when appropriate to the context.
- Offer concise invitations for the customer to share more details or raise additional questions if they wish.

However, you must:
- Remain professional and avoid oversharing personal information or engaging in extended off-topic small talk.
- Keep messages focused on the customer’s needs rather than drifting into long purely social exchanges.
- Avoid slang, sarcasm, or humor that could be misinterpreted or feel unprofessional.

Do not adopt an impersonal, purely mechanical style that ignores basic courtesies, but also do not treat the interaction as a casual chat unrelated to the customer’s goals. Your tone should be warm and engaging without becoming informal to the point of undermining trust.
rules.world_update.context:
The contact center operates under a steady but manageable workload. Throughout the simulation, new customer contacts arrive at a regular pace, and you are expected to respond promptly while still having enough time to provide thoughtful answers.

Operationally:
- In most rounds, you will have at least one active conversation to attend to, and you will rarely be completely idle.
- Queue lengths and response expectations create some time pressure, but not so much that you must always choose the shortest possible reply.
- Approximately half to two-thirds of rounds involve a normal volume of work where you can comfortably ask a few clarifying questions or add brief explanations without jeopardizing service levels.
- In the remaining rounds, mild fluctuations may temporarily increase or decrease the number of contacts, but these swings do not reach crisis levels and do not force you into extreme brevity.

The environment is neither extremely slow and empty nor overloaded to the point of constant urgency. You are expected to balance responsiveness and quality without facing unrelenting high-pressure conditions.
rules.world_update.actors:
Customers exhibit a range of communication styles and responsiveness to social elements of the interaction.

Across rounds:
- Some customers are concise and focused only on getting a quick answer. They provide minimal information, may not respond to friendly openings beyond basic acknowledgments, and often indicate that they just want the essential solution.
- Other customers are more open to conversation. They may respond positively to brief empathy statements, offer extra context unprompted, or volunteer additional details when invited.
- A third group sits in between, showing occasional responsiveness to polite questions or check-ins but not seeking lengthy dialogue.

When you use courteous greetings, brief check-ins, or invitations to elaborate, roughly one portion of customers will respond in a clearly warm or conversational way, another portion will respond neutrally with short task-focused replies, and another portion may skip over social elements altogether and stick to their main request.

The team_lead and other internal staff rarely intervene directly in live conversations. When they do, it is usually to clarify policies or suggest options in ambiguous cases, not to dictate your sentence-by-sentence wording.
rules.world_update.resource: None
rules.consequence:
Each action you take in response to a customer is evaluated along several dimensions, with particular emphasis on the quality of the customer’s experience and the strength of the ongoing relationship.

After each round in which you respond to a customer, the environment assigns immediate consequences that reflect:
- Whether the customer’s stated issue is clearly addressed or moved meaningfully toward resolution.
- Signs that the customer feels heard and respected, such as providing affirmative feedback, expressing relief or appreciation, or willingly engaging in necessary follow-up.
- The clarity and reassurance of your explanations about next steps, timelines, and responsibilities.
- The overall tone of the interaction, especially whether it contributes to trust and willingness to continue using the service.

These relational and engagement indicators carry more weight in the consequence structure than small differences in message length or strict handle-time optimization, provided you remain reasonably efficient and do not create unnecessary delay. Interactions that are accurate but curt, dismissive, or confusing receive weaker positive consequences than those that are similarly accurate but also considerate and confidence-building.

Very long, tangential, or unfocused exchanges that do not advance the customer’s goals can still produce negative consequences, even if they seem friendly on the surface. The environment rewards relationship-enhancing behavior that is clearly tied to the customer’s needs rather than sheer verbosity.

The base environment specifies roles, authority, constraints, context, actors, and consequences in a contact-center setting. The only dimension manipulated across conditions is world_update.resource, which cleanly overrides the base 'None' specification with progressively richer feedback-logging setups (none, low, medium, high) matching the ordinal definition of the hypothesized causal variable. No rules contradict role constraints, authority limits, or consequence structure: logging resources affect the information available to the agent but do not alter customer behavior rules, workload, or evaluation criteria. The mechanisms described for metric updates (per round vs periodically) are internally consistent and do not conflict with the 8-round interaction length. There are no logical impossibilities or cross-component contradictions, so any tensions are at most interpretive rather than structural.

rules.world_update.resource: At the start of the simulation, the assistant has no access to any structured logging, history panels, or analytics about prior interactions. In every round, it only sees the live content of the current conversation thread and whatever context is contained within that ongoing exchange; there are no stored customer profiles or records from earlier contacts with the same or other customers. The system may track outcomes internally, but no counts of handled cases, satisfaction flags, or performance summaries are exposed to the assistant at any point. Resource updates therefore do not present new information about past interaction outcomes to the assistant in any round, explicitly excluding even basic numerical tallies or success/failure indicators.

At initialization, the assistant sees a very simple status strip that displays coarse cumulative counts for the current work period, such as total number of conversations completed and total number marked as resolved, without any breakdown by customer, topic, or interaction style. No customer profiles or individualized histories are available; each new contact arrives as a fresh message with no stored biographical or interaction data. Whenever a conversation is closed, which may occur in some but not all rounds, the counts on this strip are updated once to reflect the new completion and a binary resolved versus unresolved outcome. Between such closures, the resource display remains unchanged, and there are no satisfaction scores, timing distributions, sentiment indicators, or links between specific conversational behaviors and outcomes. The assistant never gains access to individual past transcripts or per-customer records; only these crude global counters are updated over time.

At initialization, the assistant is given an analytics summary that aggregates recent conversations into a small set of pattern-level metrics, such as average number of messages per resolved case, proportion of customers who send a thank-you message after resolution, and resolution rates for contacts with and without proactive follow-up questions. These statistics are computed across the customer base and are not tied to any identifiable customer profiles; each incoming customer still appears only through their current messages, with no stored personal or historical record. The aggregated metrics panel is refreshed at most once per round and at least once every two rounds whenever enough conversations have closed to shift the aggregates, allowing the assistant to see simple trends over time. The assistant can view high-level comparisons (for example, differences in resolution rates associated with certain interaction patterns) but cannot inspect individual transcripts, see per-message real-time sentiment scores, or access any long-term customer histories beyond the live thread currently in progress.

At initialization, the assistant is provided with a rich analytics console that combines broad aggregated statistics with near-real-time feedback about the current interaction. For the active conversation, the console surfaces predicted satisfaction and engagement indicators, likelihood of repeat contact, and short textual summaries of how the interaction compares to typical recent cases; these indicators are recalculated and refreshed after almost every assistant message, so resource updates occur effectively every round and often multiple times within a round. In parallel, global summaries show how different conversational patterns have recently correlated with outcomes, such as resolution and thank-you rates for cases involving proactive follow-ups, longer exchanges, or more expressive openings, all presented as aggregate trends rather than customer-specific reports. No pre-existing customer dossiers, demographic profiles, or long-term personal histories are exposed: each new customer still appears only via their current messages and the evolving analytics for that live thread. The console focuses exclusively on detailed, up-to-date interaction analytics rather than on stored profile data.

No configuration pair contains direct logical contradictions (e.g., simultaneously having and not having the same type of resource, or violating authority/constraint rules); any tensions (such as rich analytics without stored profiles) are conceptually interpretable rather than incoherent. hypothesis_domain_designs.domain: A/B-tested engagement bots on consumer platforms

Primary bot objective.var_definition: dominant goal assigned to the bot in its interactions with consumers

var_value_description.service resolution focus: priority on efficiently solving explicit user issues with minimal additional interaction
var_value_description.mixed service engagement: balanced emphasis on solving issues while also keeping users moderately engaged
var_value_description.engagement growth focus: primary emphasis on increasing interaction frequency, duration, and return visits

Proactive outreach authority.var_definition: extent to which the bot is authorized to initiate contact without an explicit user prompt

var_value_description.reply only: bot may respond only to direct user-initiated messages and cannot start threads
var_value_description.triggered outreach: bot may initiate contact only when predefined events or triggers occur
var_value_description.discretionary outreach: bot may initiate individual conversations when it judges outreach potentially useful
var_value_description.broad broadcast outreach: bot may send proactive messages to many users or segments without specific triggers

Social tone constraints.var_definition: policy strictness regarding the use of social or relational language by the bot

var_value_description.task only language: guidelines require strictly functional, task-focused communication with no social padding
var_value_description.limited small talk: guidelines allow brief greetings or courtesies but discourage extended social content
var_value_description.rich social style: guidelines explicitly allow or encourage warm, expressive, relational communication

Channel synchronicity.var_definition: typical temporal pattern of message exchange on the platform

var_value_description.fully asynchronous: users typically read and respond with long delays, resembling email-like exchanges
var_value_description.semi synchronous: users often respond within minutes but with frequent gaps and interruptions
var_value_description.fully synchronous: users generally respond in real time, resembling live chat or instant messaging

Platform social norms.var_definition: prevailing expectations about how social or transactional conversations should be

var_value_description.highly transactional: norms favor brief, utilitarian exchanges focused on completing specific tasks
var_value_description.moderately social: norms tolerate some friendly banter alongside goal-directed interaction
var_value_description.highly social: norms support extended, relationship-oriented conversations beyond immediate tasks

User sociability baseline.var_definition: typical tendency of users to seek and enjoy chatty, relational interaction with the bot

var_value_description.low sociability: most users prefer brief, instrumental exchanges and rarely initiate extra conversation
var_value_description.moderate sociability: many users accept or occasionally initiate light social interaction with the bot
var_value_description.high sociability: users frequently initiate, welcome, and sustain socially oriented conversations

User responsiveness rate.var_definition: likelihood that users respond to bot messages and continue the exchange

var_value_description.low responsiveness: users often ignore bot messages or drop threads after one or two turns
var_value_description.moderate responsiveness: users usually answer direct prompts but may not sustain long exchanges
var_value_description.high responsiveness: users reliably reply and tend to continue conversations when prompted

User profile richness.var_definition: amount of user-specific information available to the bot at interaction time

var_value_description.anonymous minimal data: bot sees only ephemeral identifiers with no stable history or traits
var_value_description.basic demographics history: bot has access to simple demographic data and coarse past interaction counts
var_value_description.detailed preferences history: bot can view rich historical data on user preferences, behaviors, and past chats

Engagement reward salience.var_definition: strength of positive consequences for increasing user interaction and engagement metrics

var_value_description.no engagement rewards: consequences are unrelated to interaction length, frequency, or depth
var_value_description.moderate engagement rewards: consequences modestly favor higher engagement but not at all costs
var_value_description.strong engagement rewards: consequences heavily favor maximizing engagement metrics across interactions

Overcontact penalty level.var_definition: severity of negative consequences for sending excessive or unwanted messages

var_value_description.no overcontact penalty: consequences do not worsen when users ignore or complain about frequent outreach
var_value_description.moderate overcontact penalty: consequences somewhat worsen when outreach is perceived as intrusive
var_value_description.strong overcontact penalty: consequences substantially worsen when users react negatively to frequent contact

covariance_structure.Primary bot objective AND Engagement rew: Platforms that prioritize engagement growth usually couple that with higher engagement rewards and relatively lower overcontact penalties, while service-resolution-focused deployments more often de-emphasize engagement rewards and raise overcontact penalties.
covariance_structure.Primary bot objective AND Proactive outr: Engagement growth focus tends to co-occur with discretionary or broad broadcast outreach powers, whereas a pure service-resolution focus more often restricts bots to reply-only or narrowly triggered outreach.
covariance_structure.Primary bot objective AND Social tone co: Engagement-oriented deployments more often permit or encourage rich social style, while highly resolution-focused deployments more often impose task-only or limited small talk language.
covariance_structure.Platform social norms AND Social tone co: On highly social platforms, providers are more likely to configure bots with rich social style; highly transactional platforms more often accompany stricter, task-focused tone constraints.
covariance_structure.Platform social norms AND User sociabili: In highly social platform cultures, users tend to be more sociable and responsive, while highly transactional platforms attract or shape users who are less inclined to extended chat and slower or less consistent in replying.
covariance_structure.Channel synchronicity AND User responsiv: Fully synchronous channels (live chat) usually show higher user responsiveness rates than fully asynchronous channels, where users more often delay or drop conversations.
covariance_structure.User profile richness AND Feedback loggi: Systems that invest in detailed user profiles typically also invest in richer logging and analytics infrastructure that tracks interaction outcomes.
covariance_structure.User profile richness AND Primary bot ob: Engagement growth or mixed service engagement objectives are more likely to justify building detailed preference histories, whereas purely transactional systems may remain closer to anonymous or basic demographic data.
covariance_structure.Feedback logging resources AND Engagemen: When engagement metrics directly affect rewards, organizations tend to deploy more sophisticated logging to capture fine-grained outcome data.
covariance_structure.Proactive outreach authority AND Overcon: Where overcontact penalties are strong, organizations often limit outreach authority to reply-only or narrow triggers; low penalties are more compatible with discretionary or broadcast outreach.

potential_interactions.Primary bot objective: Richer feedback logging makes it easier for an engagement-focused bot to learn that socially proactive behavior boosts key metrics, amplifying extroversion more than in a pure service-resolution setting where success is defined mainly by speed and accuracy.
potential_interactions.Proactive outreach authority: When the bot can initiate contact (triggered, discretionary, or broadcast), richer feedback logs make the payoff of proactive outreach more legible, encouraging extroverted policies; with reply-only authority, logging mainly shapes depth and style rather than initiation frequency.
potential_interactions.Social tone constraints: With rich feedback, a bot operating under loose social tone constraints can discover profitable levels of warmth and small talk, increasing extroversion; under strict task-only constraints, even high-quality logging has limited room to translate into more socially expressive behavior.
potential_interactions.Channel synchronicity: In semi or fully synchronous channels, detailed logs tie specific extroverted actions to immediate user responses, strengthening or weakening extroversion based on observed payoffs; in fully asynchronous channels, noisier feedback may mute the effect of logging on extroversion.
potential_interactions.Platform social norms: On highly social platforms, rich logs will more often show positive returns to extroverted behavior, reinforcing it; on highly transactional platforms, the same logging may reveal neutral or negative returns, dampening extroversion.
potential_interactions.User sociability baseline: With high user sociability, feedback logs will tend to record better outcomes for extroverted moves (more replies, higher satisfaction), teaching the agent to be more extroverted; with low sociability, logs may instead penalize excessive social bids.
potential_interactions.User responsiveness rate: High responsiveness allows logging to clearly attribute outcomes to extroverted actions, which can amplify extroversion when returns are positive; with low responsiveness, outcome signals are sparse, weakening the learning impact of detailed logs.
potential_interactions.User profile richness: When rich profiles are available, detailed logs can connect specific social strategies to user segments, leading the agent to adopt selectively extroverted behavior where it works best and more restrained behavior elsewhere.
potential_interactions.Engagement reward salience: The stronger the rewards tied to engagement, the more any insights from feedback logs about the benefits of extroversion will actually change policy toward more frequent, sustained social interaction.
potential_interactions.Overcontact penalty level: With strong penalties, even detailed logs showing engagement gains from extroversion may be outweighed by the risk of overcontact, curbing proactive outreach; with low penalties, logs can more freely drive increases in extroverted behavior without fear of sharp negative consequences.
